title: Paragraph IV Notice Letter: Requirements, Timing, and Checklist
summary: Use this Paragraph IV notice letter checklist for required content, ANDA and 505(b)(2) timing, recipients, service, receipt proof, and FDA follow-up.
body_markdown:
A Paragraph IV notice letter is a regulated litigation work product. It must identify the application and patents, explain every challenged claim, reach the correct recipients on time, and leave an acceptable proof record. Each required recipient's receipt of a valid, complete notice starts that recipient's separate 45-day period, except for a later-listed patent, where the period does not apply.


The checklists separate the rules for abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs) and § 505(b)(2) applications and connect the letter to immediate FDA consequences.


> **Legal information only.** This page provides general federal legal and FDA procedural information. It is not legal advice, does not create an attorney-client relationship, and cannot account for every matter's facts. Law, FDA procedure, court orders, and matter-specific facts can change the result. We rechecked the linked primary federal sources on August 28, 2026. Consult qualified counsel and current primary sources before acting.


## Key takeaways


- The certification goes to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The notice letter goes to the required patent-side recipients after the applicable filing event.
- An original ANDA notice sent before receipt of FDA's Paragraph IV acknowledgment letter is invalid. It is also invalid if sent before the first working day after the patent appears in the Orange Book.
- The detailed statement requires a full factual and legal explanation for each claim alleged to be invalid, unenforceable, or not infringed.
- The recipient and delivery records matter as much as the analysis. FDA specifies who must receive notice and what evidence proves sending and receipt.
- Each required recipient's receipt of a valid, complete notice starts that recipient's separate 45-day period. The period does not apply to the later-listed patents covered by the regulatory exception.
- A timely suit can delay final approval for 30 months or, in the five-year new-chemical-entity setting, until 7.5 years after NDA approval. Court decisions and orders can change that date in defined ways.


## What is a Paragraph IV notice letter?


A Paragraph IV certification states that an Orange Book-listed patent is invalid or will not be infringed by the proposed drug. It is submitted in an ANDA under § 505(j) or a § 505(b)(2) application. The separate letter gives required recipients the factual and legal basis for seeking approval before patent expiration.


Under[35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(2)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title35-section271&num=0&edition=prelim) , submission of a covered ANDA or § 505(b)(2) application is an artificial act of infringement when the applicant seeks approval, before the relevant patent expires, to engage in commercial manufacture, use, or sale of a drug claimed in that patent or for a patented use for which approval is sought. The letter communicates the patent challenge. It is often shortened to **PIV notice letter** . Searches for **Paragraph 4 notice letter** and **ANDA notice letter** usually refer to the same work product, although § 505(b)(2) applicants also use the notice process.


## What must the notice letter contain?


The two paths have parallel requirements, with different statutory citations and application-status statements.[21 C.F.R. § 314.95(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-314/subpart-C/section-314.95#p-314.95(c)) governs ANDA notices.[21 C.F.R. § 314.52(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-314/subpart-B/section-314.52#p-314.52(c)) governs § 505(b)(2) notices.


Content Original ANDA notice Original § 505(b)(2) notice


Governing statutory citation Cite § 505(j)(2)(B)(iv) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Cite § 505(b)(3)(D).


Application status State that FDA received the ANDA containing any required bioavailability or bioequivalence information and that the applicant received its Paragraph IV acknowledgment letter. State that the § 505(b)(2) application containing any required bioavailability or bioequivalence studies was submitted and filed by FDA.


Application identifier ANDA number NDA number


Proposed drug Established name, active ingredient, strength, and dosage form Established name, active ingredient, strength, and dosage form


Patents Patent number and expiration date for each listed patent alleged invalid, unenforceable, or not infringed Same requirement for each patent on the list


Detailed statement For each claim alleged not infringed, a full explanation of why; for each claim alleged invalid or unenforceable, a full explanation of the grounds Same claim-by-claim requirement


Offer of confidential access Required with a noninfringement notice if the applicant wants to preserve the statutory option for a later declaratory-judgment action Parallel requirement for the § 505(b)(2) application


U.S. process agent Name and address of a U.S. agent authorized to accept service if the applicant lacks a U.S. residence or place of business Same requirement


The governing statutes also require notice that the application seeks approval to engage in commercial manufacture, use, or sale before expiration of the patent.


### Build the detailed statement claim by claim


The detailed statement is the substantive core of the letter. Separate every patent, claim, and ground. For noninfringement, record the construction, relevant application feature or proposed labeling, missing limitation, and support. For invalidity, record the legal ground, prior art or intrinsic evidence, limitation mapping, and facts supporting the theory.


Give a supportable position without copying unnecessary confidential formulation or manufacturing detail into the letter. FDA has treated notice letters as public disclosures, and the[Nycomed v. Tolmar court](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-njd-2_10-cv-02635/pdf/USCOURTS-njd-2_10-cv-02635-0.pdf) held that the letter and detailed statement were outside a discovery confidentiality order. The offer of confidential access protects the separate application-access process. It does not automatically protect the notice.


Later litigation is not categorically limited to the letter's theories. In a March 30, 2023 opinion on Rule 12 motions, the Northern District of West Virginia held in[Bausch v. Mylan](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-wvnd-1_22-cv-00020/pdf/USCOURTS-wvnd-1_22-cv-00020-1.pdf) that it would not limit Mylan to the noninfringement theories in its notice letter when deciding a motion for judgment on the pleadings. Mylan could develop those contentions in the ordinary course of that case. This limited district-court holding does not establish a broadly controlling rule about notice-letter scope or excuse a weak starting position. In[Takeda v. Mylan](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/07-1269.pdf) , the Federal Circuit affirmed an exceptional-case fee award based on baseless certification letters compounded by litigation misconduct, while making clear that ordinary development of a theory alone was not the problem.

## When must the applicant send notice?


The original-application and later-amendment rules are different. The exact rules appear in[§§ 314.95(b) and (d)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-314/subpart-C/section-314.95#p-314.95(b)) for ANDAs and[§§ 314.52(b) and (d)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-314/subpart-B/section-314.52#p-314.52(b)) for § 505(b)(2) applications.


Filing posture Earliest valid notice Outer deadline


Paragraph IV certification in an original ANDA On or after the applicant receives FDA's Paragraph IV acknowledgment letter, and no earlier than the first working day after the patent is published in the Orange Book No later than 20 days after the acknowledgment letter's postmark. The count starts the next day, with a weekend and federal-holiday extension for day 20.


Paragraph IV certification in an original § 505(b)(2) application On or after FDA's applicable filing date under § 314.101(a)(2) or (3). Notice sent before that filing date is invalid. No later than 20 days after the Paragraph IV acknowledgment letter's postmark, using the same counting rule.


Paragraph IV certification added to an ANDA after an acknowledgment letter At the same time the amendment or supplement is submitted to FDA Simultaneous with the submission


Paragraph IV certification added to a § 505(b)(2) application after its applicable filing date At the same time the amendment or supplement is submitted to FDA Simultaneous with the submission


If an ANDA amendment adds the certification before the applicant receives its acknowledgment letter, notice follows the original-ANDA timing rule. The parallel § 505(b)(2) rule applies when an amendment adds the certification before the applicable filing date.


## Who must receive notice?


For each challenged patent, the applicant must send notice to:


- **each patent owner or the representative designated by that owner to receive notice; and**
- **the approved NDA holder for the listed drug.** If the NDA holder does not reside or maintain a place of business in the United States, notice instead goes to the NDA holder's U.S. attorney, agent, or other authorized official.


The patent owner or designated representative address comes from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office record. FDA's Orange Book Staff provides the NDA holder or specified U.S. recipient information. No notice is required for a method-of-use patent that does not claim a use for which the applicant seeks approval.


## How must notice be served and documented?


Notice must travel by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested, or by a designated delivery service meeting FDA's definition. An alternative method requires FDA agreement in advance.


Within 30 days after the last required recipient receives notice, the applicant must amend its ANDA or § 505(b)(2) application with:


- evidence of the date notice was sent within the applicable timing rule;
- evidence of each recipient's receipt date, using a return receipt, signature proof of delivery from a designated delivery service, or a letter acknowledging receipt; and
- for an ANDA, a dated printout of the Orange Book entry for the reference listed drug showing the patent that is the subject of the certification.


The amendment also certifies that notice reached every required person and met the content requirements. The notice copy itself need not be submitted to FDA under §§ 314.95(b)(3) and (e) or the parallel provisions in § 314.52.


### The Minocin delivery dispute shows what signature proof means


A designated-service signature proof is acceptable. The Minocin defect was a FedEx slip marked “C-19” under a contactless-delivery practice instead of bearing the recipient or designated representative signature. The[District of Columbia district court](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-dcd-1_22-cv-02190/pdf/USCOURTS-dcd-1_22-cv-02190-0.pdf) held that the slip did not satisfy § 314.95(e), vacated FDA's approval, and remanded. FDA later determined that receipt occurred on March 31, 2021, and issued a[post-remand tentative approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/214934Orig1s000TA_ltr.pdf) .


## What happens during the 45-day period?


Each required recipient's receipt of a valid, complete notice starts that recipient's separate 45-day period on the following day. The recipients are each patent owner or owner-designated representative and the NDA holder. If the NDA holder lacks a U.S. residence or place of business, the rule applies to its specified U.S. attorney, agent, or authorized official. If day 45 falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, it moves to the next non-holiday weekday. FDA may count from a later date if the applicant provides the written statement allowed by § 314.95(f), or amends its § 505(b)(2) application with the statement allowed by § 314.52(f). For a patent covered by the later-listed-patent exception discussed below, no 45-day period applies.


For a patent listed before the application was submitted, a suit filed in time by the **patent owner, its representative, or exclusive patent licensee** generally delays final approval until 30 months after the later date on which any listed patent owner or its representative, or the NDA holder or its representative, received notice. A court may shorten or extend the period if either side fails to cooperate reasonably in expediting the action.


A five-year new-chemical-entity case has a different measure. If the suit is brought within 45 days and during the one-year period beginning four years after NDA approval, the bar can run until 7.5 years after that approval. Qualifying pediatric exclusivity changes the statutory references from four years, 48 months, and 7.5 years to 4.5 years, 54 months, and eight years, respectively.[21 U.S.C. § 355a](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title21-section355a&num=0&edition=prelim) supplies those pediatric extensions.


[Section 314.107(b)(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-314/subpart-D/section-314.107#p-314.107(b)(3)) defines the events that can change the approval date:


- A district court judgment of invalidity, unenforceability, or noninfringement permits approval on the judgment date. A court-entered settlement order or consent decree with the same finding has the same effect.
- If the district court finds infringement and the judgment is appealed, approval follows an appellate mandate, settlement order, or consent decree finding invalidity, unenforceability, or noninfringement. If the infringement judgment is not appealed or is affirmed, approval cannot occur before the date in the district court's § 271(e)(4)(A) order.
- A preliminary injunction follows the applicable final-decision path once the court decides validity and infringement.
- Written consent from the patent owner or exclusive patent licensee permits approval on or after the consent date.
- A court order terminating the 30-month or 7.5-year period controls according to its terms.
- If every timely infringement suit is dismissed, with or without prejudice and without an infringement finding, approval may occur on or after the dismissal order.


The later-listed-patent exception remains important. When the NDA holder submits the patent information after the ANDA or § 505(b)(2) application was submitted, the applicant still may need a certification, notice, and receipt documentation. The 45-day period does not apply, and § 314.107(b)(2) permits approval upon submission of the receipt documentation if the application is otherwise eligible.


The applicant must notify FDA within 14 days after any action filed within a recipient's applicable 45-day period and report the specified judgments, orders, appeals, injunctions, or written consent within the applicable 14-day period. If no timely suit is reported, FDA may require the applicant to confirm that none was filed before approval after the applicable 45-day periods or completion of review, whichever is later.


## Paragraph IV notice letter checklist for applicants


- Classify the certification as part of the original application or a later amendment or supplement.
- Record the earliest valid service date and the 20-day or simultaneous-notice deadline.
- Audit every required content field against § 314.95(c) or § 314.52(c).
- Review the detailed statement by patent, claim, ground, construction, fact, and source.
- Separate public letter content from material reserved for confidential application access.
- Identify each patent owner or owner-designated representative and the NDA holder. If the NDA holder lacks a U.S. residence or place of business, identify its specified U.S. attorney, agent, or authorized official.
- Use a permitted delivery method and retain acceptable evidence of sending and signed receipt.
- Within 30 days after the last receipt, submit the required FDA amendment, including the dated Orange Book entry printout for an ANDA. Do not submit the letter itself.
- Docket a separate 45-day period from each required recipient's receipt of a valid, complete notice and record any written statement asking FDA to use a later date. For a later-listed patent covered by the exception, record that no 45-day period applies.
- Report a timely suit and later court events or written consent to FDA within the required periods.


## Immediate intake checklist for recipients


- Preserve the letter, detailed statement, envelope, attachments, tracking history, and signed delivery record.
- Record receipt separately for each patent owner or owner-designated representative and for the NDA holder. If the NDA holder lacks a U.S. residence or place of business, record receipt by its specified U.S. attorney, agent, or authorized official.
- Docket the separate 45-day period triggered by each required recipient's receipt of a valid, complete notice, including the weekend and federal-holiday rule. For a later-listed patent covered by the exception, record that no 45-day period applies.
- Identify every application, drug strength, dosage form, patent, claim, and asserted ground in the notice.
- Route the letter immediately to patent litigation, regulatory, and responsible in-house teams.
- Review any[offer of confidential access](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?edition=prelim&num=0&req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title21-section355) before requesting application material because the request accepts the stated restrictions.
- Record whether each patent was listed before or after the application submission date.
- If a suit is filed, coordinate the notice to FDA. The applicant has the mandatory 14-day duty, and the patent owner or NDA holder may also notify FDA.
